text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike in 5xxs from model-hosting pool 'mh-eu-1' — error rate 18% over last 5m, latency 2x baseline. Pager routed to @maria-oncall. Logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/q/1763509123

maria-oncall: I'm on it. pulling recent graphs and pod list. first confirm customer impact?

jinx-eng: Seeing a lot of model-runner exits (OOM killer) and segfault lines in node logs. Repro on a couple of pods.

sam-sre: I can take infra side—checking node memory pressure and recent kube evictions. Running: `kubectl get pods -n infer -o wide --selector=pool=mh-eu-1`

anya-ml: Which model variants are hot? My quick slice shows traffic routed to gptx-30b-qat at ~25% quantized path. Might be hitting a kernel path with mem corruption.

lee-support: Customer impact: 14 active customers reporting errors via status page, most hit timeouts or 502 gateway. Escalating to AE for top 3.

jinx-eng: Pasting stack snippets from one runner:
```
[pid 8241] signal 11 (SEGV), code 1 (SEGV_MAPERR) at 0x7fffb5c0
backtrace:
  model_runner() [0x55a1f2b7]
  kv_cache_get() [0x55a1f3e2]
  attention_kernel() [0x55a1a8c4]
  ...
```

maria-oncall: Good capture. Sam, can you cordon the worst nodes and restart the daemonset for the pool? Jinx, please try running model runner with --disable-quant-path on one canary pod.

sam-sre: cordoned node ip-10-2-4-9, draining one pod. Restarting daemonset now: `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/model-runner -n infer --field-selector=spec.nodeName=ip-10-2-4-9`

ops-bot: Deploy triggered by @sam-sre — rollout ID rl-2026-176350. Watch: https://deploys.redwood.internal/rl-2026-176350

anya-ml: Canary with --disable-quant-path started, traffic mirrored. Early signs: that pod handled several requests without segfault. Might be quant kernel related.

jinx-eng: Confirmed: canary stayed healthy for 6m while others crashed. Full stack shows crash in quant attention kernel (avx512 path).

lee-support: Notifying top customers: "We're investigating elevated errors; routing to fallback models where possible." Sending updates to impacted customers now.

maria-oncall: Plan: 1) Disable quantized kernel on pool (hotpatch flag), 2) Reroute new sessions to dedicated fallback pool (mh-eu-dedicated-small) for high-SLA customers, 3) Continue node drains to remove corrupted kernel drivers. Any objections? :thumbsup: or :thumbsdown:

sam-sre: +1. I'll open a host-level ticket to repro kernel mismatch with driver team.

anya-ml: +1. Also recommend temporary autoscale increase on fallback pool to handle surge: scaling policy bump x2 for 20m.

jinx-eng: Hotpatch command (dry-run shown):
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/pools/mh-eu-1/hotpatch \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"kernel_overrides": {"quant_attention": "disable"}}'
```
Executing now.

maria-oncall: Ops-bot shows patch applied. Watching metrics.

incident-bot: Patch applied to mh-eu-1. Error rate dropping to 6% in 3m window.

lee-support: Customer update sent — pushing to AEs for follow-up. Some customers accepted fallback pool; a couple requested rollout revert only after postmortem.

sam-sre: Nodes with driver mismatch identified: 3 hosts with older libkern build. Opening infra PR to standardize images and schedule rolling kernel-redeploy.

jinx-eng: We'll prepare a minimal revertable runtime patch for quant kernel rewrite. For now keep quant disabled and monitor.

maria-oncall: Current status: error rate 2.1%, latency trending to baseline. Keeping page open for 45m observation window. Assigning follow-ups: `jinx-eng` (runtime fix), `sam-sre` (host repro & kernel rollout), `anya-ml` (regression tests with quant variants), `lee-support` (customer comms).

ops-bot: Follow-up ticket created: INC-2026-7342 with actions and links to logs/graphs.

lee-support: Logged impacted customers list and sent initial credit offers to top impacted tenants.

maria-oncall: Thanks team. If anything regresses, re-escalate to oncall rotation. Closing channel when monitoring window finishes. :white_check_mark:
